replacement.title: Change jobs after the turnover
replacement.objective: Switch from attacking support to defensive recovery when possession changes.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x). Gold D1 has won control, so gold now attacks the left net (-x). YOU and navy F1 must change from attacking support to defence. Gold F2 trails D1 on the other side of the middle.
cues: Gold D1 now owns the puck.
Gold F2 is a separate trailing option across the middle.

questions.prompt: What fact changes your earlier attacking plan?

options.text: D1 has won the puck
F2 is on the other side of the middle
YOU are closer to the left net than navy F1

questions.explanation: D1 is the new puck owner, so the possession relationship has changed.

questions.prompt: Which two cues shape your new defensive job?

options.text: D1's direction with the puck
F2's route toward the left net
The old support lane as if Navy still had possession

questions.explanation: The new carrier and second attacker set the recovery problem; the old attacking plan is stale.

questions.prompt: Put this turnover response in order.

options.text: Recognize D1 has possession
Find F2 and the left net
Choose a recovery relationship

questions.explanation: The job changes at the turnover, then the route is chosen from the new threat picture.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the defended left net, then recheck D1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU closer to the left net. D1 is still nearer that net than YOU; keep reading both gold attackers rather than assuming you have recovered ahead of the carrier.

questions.prompt: Navy F1 gains control back from D1 before gold F2 receives. What changes first?

options.text: Re-check possession and return to an attacking support read
Continue backchecking F2 without looking
Assume F2 still controls the puck

questions.explanation: F1 is your navy teammate. Confirm that regain and look for attacking support toward the right net, while checking gold pressure.

questions.prompt: How can one skater have two jobs within a few seconds?
questions.explanation: A turnover changes the puck carrier and direction. Explain how the same visible teammates require attacking support before the turnover and defensive recovery after it.

questions.prompt: What is the puck state at this freeze?

options.text: Navy controls it
Gold controls it
It is loose

questions.explanation: The puck is loose at centre ice; neither team has established control.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should YOU watch?

options.text: Which centre gains control
How F2 can support navy possession or help defend gold possession
The faceoff label alone

questions.explanation: First identify the controlling player and team. F2 is navy, so the useful job changes with possession.

questions.prompt: Arrange the after-faceoff read.

options.text: Read the centre contest and nearby space
Identify who controls the puck and their team
Choose support for navy possession or defence against gold

questions.explanation: Keep reading while possession is uncertain. Once control is clear, choose a role that matches the team with the puck.

questions.prompt: Move YOU farther from the centre contest while keeping room to react.
questions.explanation: The example leaves more distance from both centres. Keep scanning the puck and F2; this position alone does not guarantee a passing lane or defensive coverage.

questions.prompt: Gold C2 gains clean control. What should update first?

options.text: YOU should scan the defensive route toward the left net
Hold the same navy second-play spot
Assume F2 has the puck

questions.explanation: Gold possession changes the direction and job; re-read C2, F2, and the left-net route.

questions.prompt: How should uncertain possession change your support call?
questions.explanation: Call that the puck is loose and keep scanning while leaving room for the contest. If navy gains control, offer support; if gold gains control, communicate a defensive response. You do not need to stand still while waiting to identify control.

questions.prompt: Why do YOU have a different first job from F2?

options.text: F2 is closer to the loose puck
YOU own the puck
D1 is a navy player

questions.explanation: F2 is slightly closer to the loose puck than YOU and has the retrieval assignment. D1 is closer still; distances alone do not prove who arrives or gains control first.

questions.prompt: Which two checks support a slot-side position?

options.text: Whether an outlet would be reachable if F2 gains control
Whether D1 follows F2 or leaves space
Being closest to the puck at all times

questions.explanation: Look for a possible outlet without crowding the retrieval. F2 does not yet control the puck, so recheck D1 before assuming a pass is available.

questions.prompt: Arrange this corner-support response.

options.text: Read F2, D1 and the net
Hold a slot-side support angle
Recheck who gains control and update the job

questions.explanation: Leave room for the retrieval while scanning D1. Offer an outlet if F2 gains control, or change to defence if D1 does.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the middle to offer a possible outlet for F2.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU nearer the middle and farther from F2. It may leave room for an outlet if F2 gains control, but the pass and D1’s response still need checking.

questions.prompt: D1 wins the puck and carries out of the corner. What changes for YOU?

options.text: Change to defence and read D1’s route toward the left net
Keep planning a pass from F2 despite D1’s control
Chase the old loose-puck spot

questions.explanation: D1 is a gold opponent. With D1 in control, coordinate with F2 to defend the left-net route rather than continuing the attacking support plan.

questions.prompt: How can YOU help the retrieval without being closest?
questions.explanation: A middle-side support angle can leave F2 room and offer an outlet if F2 gains control and the lane stays clear. Keep checking D1; a pass is not guaranteed.
